ऐण्डिल: Aiṇḍila m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Kauravya, one of those offered in the snake-sacrifice 1. 52. 12, 1, 11.
ऐरावण: Airāvaṇa m.: A lordly mythical ele-phant. A. Vehicle of Indra (इन्द्रवाह्य) 9. 19. 11, 5. B. Used as standard of comparison— for Śālva's elephant 9. 19. 11, (6, 1-2); for the elephant dispatched by the king of the Magadha against Abhimanyu's chariot 6. 58. 42; for elephants from the northern mountain born in the family of Añjana 7. 87. 24, 34. C. Many elephants born in the family of Airāvaṇa killed by Sātyaki in the great war 7. 97. 25, 20. [See Airāvata2.]
ऐरावत: Airāvata1 m.: A mythical king of serpents (नागराज 6. 86. 6) living in Bhoga-vatī Purī 5. 101. 11, 1. A. Birth: Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 5. B. Children: His son (not named) picked up the कुण्डलस्, given to Uttaṅka by Madayantī, and entered the नागलोक 14. 57. 39 (ऐरावतसुत), 22 (ऐरावतकुलोत्पन्न) [According to 1. 3. 136 ff. the कुण्डलस् were taken away by Takṣaka]; Airāvata gave his widowed daughter (not named, Ulūpī ?; but cf. the next) to Arjuna in marriage 6. 86. 6-8. C. Descendants: Founder of a family (कुल) 1. 52. 11; Kauravya, father of Ulūpī born in Airāvata's कुल 1. 206. 18; Sumukha, son of Cikura, was born in his कुल 5. 101. 23; serpents living in the नागलोक described as born in the family of Airavata (ऐरावतोद्-भवाः), who have Airāvata as their king (ऐरावतराजानः), and whose eldest brother is Airāvata (ऐरावतज्येष्ठभ्रातृभ्यः … नमः) 1, 3. 140, 139. 143; his descendants (ऐरावताः) sided with Arjuna when mythi-cal beings, gathered in the sky, took sides between Karṇa and Arjuna 8. 63. 37. D. An arrow from the वंश of Airāvata: A fierce, burning arrow having a serpent at its sharp point (सर्पमुख शर), very poi-sonous (महाविष) [on which Aśvasena, son of Takṣaka, lay 8. 66. 23], and which was reserved by Karṇa to be shot at Arjuna described as belonging to the वंश of Airāvata (ऐरावतवंशसंभव) 8. 66. 5, 6. E. Importance: He is one of the guardians of Bhogavatī Purī 5. 107. 19; one of the नागस् who wait on Varuṇa in his सभा 2. 9. 8; Sumukha chosen as bride-groom for Guṇakeśī, daughter of Mātali, out of regard for Airāvata 5. 102. 10; Vāsuki consulted him, together with others, who were all धर्मपरायण how to neutralize the curse uttered by their mother on them 1. 33. 2; Ut-taṅka said no one would want to move in the army of the enemies unless Airāvata accom-panied them 1. 3. 141. F. Events: (i) His dwelling (निवेशन) filled with smoke when Uttaṅka blew into the anus of a horse 14. 57. 47; (ii) He and Citra were agitated on hearing the roar of Skanda; when Skanda saw Airāvata and Citra approa-ching he caught them in his hands 3. 214. 22, 23.

Airāvata2 m.: A lordly mythical ele-phant. A. Birth and Origin: Son of Bhadra-manā (daughter of Tāmrā ? 1. 60. 54) 1. 60. 61; born in the वंश of Supratīka 5. 97. 15; produced by Kṛṣṇa along with clouds and lightning 13. 143. 36. B. Description: White in colour, had four tusks (चतुर्दन्त); hence looked like mount Kailāsa with its peak (?) 3. 43. 36; well-tamed and covered with lustre all around 6. 60. 52; 12. 220. 10; endowed with good marks (लक्षणैर् युतम्) 5. 18. 1; decorated with two bells (घण्टा) called Vaijayantī which were given by Indra to Guha 3. 220. 18. C. Status: Celestial elephant (देवनाग) 1. 60. 61; king of elephants (नागराज) 1. 3. 174, (गजराज) 12. 220. 116, best among elephants 9. 97. 15 (वारणसत्तम), 12. 220. 13 (द्विपश्रे-ष्ट्ःअ), 5. 18. 1 (द्विपेन्द्र), 12. 220. 10 (वारणेन्द्र); as the best among the lordly elephants counted as one of the विभूतिस् of Bhagavān 6. 32. 27; Airāvata, with his followers, came to attend the अभिषेक of Skanda 9. 44. 13; the way to the residence of Kubera from the Gandhamādana mountain named after him (ऐरावतपथ) 3. 159. 31. D. Cosmographical function: Mentioned among the four दिग्गजस् 6. 13. 33; 6. 60. 50. E. Association with Indra: Vehicle of Indra (महेन्द्रवाह) 9. 16. 51; Indra called गजराजवाहन 12. 220. 116; bull and a man seen by Uttaṅka were Airāvata and Indra 1. 3. 174; after the fall of Nahuṣa, Indra seated on Airāvata roamed the three worlds 5. 18. 1; seated on Airāvata Indra went over the earth in search of Bali 12. 216. 11; 12. 220. 10, 12, 13; when Śiva proceeded towards Bhadra-vaṭa, Indra, riding Airāvata, followed him 3. 221. 6; riding on Airāvata Indra arrived to meet Arjuna to invite him to heaven 3. 42. 13; Arjuna saw Airāvata at the gate of Amarāvatī 3. 43. 36; Indra took Airāvata out also in battles, e. g. in his fight against Skanda 3. 216. 3; hence Bhagadatta fighting from his elephant Supratīka compared with Indra fighting from his Airāvata 5. 164 38; 6. 91. 33; Abhimanyu boasted that he would fight even against Indra on his Airāvata 7. 35. 6. F. Standard of comparison: Śālva's huge, mountain like elephant, born in the family of Mahābhadra (9. 19. 3), compared with Airāvata 9. 19. 2, 6; Śalya compared with Airāvata (महेन्द्रवाहप्रतिम) 9. 16. 51, 52. G. Myths and Miracles: Airāvata takes water from पाताल and puts it into the clouds which Indra then sends down as rain 5. 97. 7; the bull seen by Uttaṅka on his way to king Pauṣya in order to fetch the कुण्डलस् was Airāvata 1. 3. 174; what Upamanyu saw as Airāvata on whom Indra was seated turned into a bull on whom Maheśvara and Umā sat 13. 14. 105, 110; Ghaṭotkaca created Airāvata with his माया, rode on him, and attacked Bhagadatta 6. 60. 50, 53; this Airā-vata, created with the help of माया, attacked Bhagadatta's elephant 6. 60. 54. [See Airāvaṇa]

Airāvata nt.: Name of a Varṣa. A. Location: It lay beyond the Śveta and the Hairaṇyaka Varṣa and beyond the Śṛṅgavant mountain (श्वेताद् धैरण्यकं परम् । वर्षम् ऐरावतं नाम ततः शृङ्गवतः परम्) 6. 7. 35; beyond the Śṛṅgavant mountain it reached up to the ocean (उत्तरेण तु शृङ्गस्य समुद्रान्ते जनाधिप । वर्षम् ऐरावतं नाम तस्माच् छृङ्गवतः परम्) 6. 9. 10. B. Chara-cteristics: Among the seven Varṣas, be-ginning with the Bhāratavarṣa in the south and ending with the Airāvata in the north (in between lay Haimavata, Hari, Ilāvṛta, Śveta and Hairaṇyaka, See Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 37-38), each succeeding one excelled its immediately preceding one in the dura-tion of life, in health, as well as in quali-ties related to धर्म, काम and अर्थ; people lived there in association with one other (उत्तरोत्तरम् एतेभ्यो वर्षम् उद्रि-च्यते गुणैः । आयुष्प्रमाणम् आरोग्यम् धर्मतः कामतो ऽर्थतः ॥ समन्वितानि भूतानि तेषु वर्षेषु भारत) 6. 7. 37-38 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 40: समन्वितानि भिन्नभावेन संगतानि ?); the sun does not get hot there, men do not grow old, the moon, together with the नक्षत्रस्, is as though all light; men are born there having the brightness, colour and fragrance of lotus, and having eyes like lotus leaves; their eyes do not wink, they are fragrant, they live without food, and have control over their sense-organs; they are all descend-ed from the world of gods and are free from the quality of passion; their life span is of thirteen thousand years (न तत्र सूर्यस् तपति न ते जीर्यन्ति मानवाः । चन्द्रमाश् च सनक्षत्रो ज्योतिर्भूत इवावृतः ॥ पद्म-प्रभाः पद्मवर्णाः पद्मपत्रनिभेक्ष-णाः । पद्मपत्रसुगन्धाश् च जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः ॥ अनिष्पन्दा सुगन्धाश् च निरा-हारा जितेन्द्रियाः । देवलोकच्युताः सर्वे तथा विरजसो नृप ॥ त्रयोदश सहस्राणि वर्षाणां ते जनाधिप । आयुष्प्रमाणं जीवन्ति नरा भरतसत्तम ॥ ) 6. 9. 11-14.
ऐन्द्रास्त्र: Aindrāstra (ऐन्द्रम् अस्त्रम्) nt.: Name of a missile special to Indra; also known as Indrāstra, Māhendrāstra, Śakrāstra. A. Users: According to Bhīṣma, known to Arjuna and (perhaps) to Kṛṣṇa 6. 116. 38; but it was known to Droṇa 7. 166. 2; Mādhava (Sātyaki) learnt it from Vijaya (Arjuna) 6. 78. 39; it was once used even by Yudhiṣṭhira 7. 132. 32. B. Description: heavenly (दिव्य) 4. 58. 8, an excellent missile (अस्त्रवर 6. 55. 120; उत्तमास्त्र 6. 55. 111); bright like the sun (आदित्यसं-काश) 4. 58. 8; extremely terrible (सुघोर) 6. 55. 110, 127; destructive like the end of the aeon (युगान्तकल्प) 6. 55. 127. C. Mode of use: Certain मन्त्रस् were recited over the bow, the bow-string, and the arrow at the time of releasing it (अभिन्यमन्त्र-यत् 8. 66. 48; अनुमन्त्र्य 8. 66. 49), follow-ing certain prescriptions (विधिवत् 6. 55. 110); the verb often used with regard to its use is ‘to bring forth, to manifest’ (प्रादुष्कृ) 6. 55. 110; 7. 68. 21; 7. 132. 31, 32; 8. 19. 22; 8. 37. 31; (उद् ईरय) 6. 77. 40. D. Effect: Its primary effect was to produce a shower of arrows by releasing a single arrow 6. 55. 111, (120); 6. 77. 41; 6. 78. 37, 40; 7. 68. 21; 8. 19. 22; 8. 37. 31; 8. 66. 49; (4. 58. 9); the arrows became hard like वज्र 3. 168. 2; the arrows (due to the effect of the मन्त्रस्) became lustrous (तेजोमया बाणाः) 8. 66. 50, or appeared like bright fire (विम-लाग्निवर्ण) 6. 55. 111; when released the missile gave rise to a wonderful sight in the mid-region (प्रादुश्चकाराद्भुतम् अन्त-रिक्षे 6. 55. 110). E. Its use (princi-pally by Arjuna): (1) In the epic war: (i) When Arjuna was attacked by Bhīṣma, Duryodhana, Bhūriśravas and Śalya, he put to use the Māhendra astra by forcefully drawing the Gāṇḍīva bow 6. 55. 106-110; (ii) when Arjuna was sur-rounded by thousands of kings (राजस-हस्राणि 6. 77. 32) and his normal arrows were not enough to ward off their arrows, Arjuna brought forth his Aindra astra and successfully repelled the arrows of the enemies 6. 77. 40-41; (iii) when Arjuna was attacked by Śrutāyus and Acyutāyus who showered arrows on the right and left of Arjuna and attacked him with तोमर and शूल respectively, Arjuna manifested Śākra astra to take care of the weapons of the enemies and kill both of them 7. 68. 7-13, 21; (iii) when attacked by the Saṃśaptakas all together, Arjuna manifested Aindra astra to cut down all sorts of weapons of the enemies as also to cut off their limbs and chariots 8. 19. 22-29; (iv) when Arjuna was severely struck on his chest by Suśar-man, he produced Aindra astra 8. 37. 30-31; (v) used by Arjuna to combat Karṇa's Brahmāstra 8. 66. 48-50; (vi) used by Arjuna to combat the Aindra astra used by Droṇa 7. 163. 28; (vii) used, together with Vāyavya, by Droṇa against Yudhiṣṭhira; the latter combated both of them with Māhendra astra 7. 132. 31, 32; (viii) used by Sātyaki to fight with the demon Alambusa; it reduced to ashes the माया employed by the demon 6. 78. 40; (2) Outside the epic war: (i) During the cattle raid, when Arjuna was attacked by Kṛpa, Karṇa and Droṇa with heavenly missiles, Arjuna released the Aindra astra; he covered the enemies with arrows as the sun would do with his rays 4. 58. 8-9; (ii) when Arjuna was attacked by the Nīvātakavacas with showers of huge rocks, Arjuna released it (Indrāstra) and the वज्र-like arrows released by the missile, pounded the rocks hurled by the enemies to pieces by hundreds 3. 168. 2. F. Status: Inferior to the Pāśupatāstra of Śiva 13. 14. 127.
ऐषीक: Aiṣīka nt.: Name of a missile. Described as a powerful missile (पर-मास्त्र); employed by Aśvatthāman to kill the foetus in the womb of Uttarā 1. 1. 154. [See Iṣīkā].

Aiṣīka nt.: Name of the 79th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 61, 30, 70. Described as very frightful (सुदारुण) 1. 2. 61; it is said to be the continuation of the Sauptikaparvan (सौप्तिकैषीकसं-बन्धे पर्वणि) 1. 2. 190; referred to in Dhṛtarāṣṭra's summary made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 154-156; it comprises the last nine अध्यायस् of the Sauptikaparvan 10. 10-18.
ऐल: Aila m.: Name of a class of Kṣatriyas. To show that the lustre and strength of illustrious Kṣatriyas was pacified by Brāhmaṇas, it was pointed out by Bhīṣma that Bharadvāja defeated Vaitahavyas and Ailas (भरद्वाजो वैतहव्यान् ऐलांश् च) 13. 34. 16. [See the next].
ऐलवंश: Ailavaṃśa m. (sg.), Ailavaṃśya (pl.): The lineage of Aila, those born in the lineage of Aila. Many kings, great heroes and godlike, were born in the dynasty of Manu; they pro-spered the lineage of Aila (i. e. of Purūra-vas 1. 90. 7) (देवकल्पा महारथाः । जाता मनोर् अन्ववाये ऐलवंशविवर्धनाः) 1. 89. 55; Kings and Kṣatriyas claim their succession either from the lineage of Aila or from Ikṣvāku; the kings born in the line-age of Aila and Ikṣvāku together make up one hundred and one families of Kṣatriyas (ऐलस्येक्ष्वाकुवंशस्य प्रकृतिं परिचक्-षते । राजानः श्रेणिबद्धाश् च ततो ऽन्ये क्षत्रिया भुवि ॥ ऐलवंश्यास् तु ये राजंस् तथैवेक्ष्वाकवो नृपाः । तानि चैकशतं विद्धि कुलानि भरतर्षभ ॥ (2. 13. 4-5).
